original_prompt:
ulw build these five independent backend modules simultaneously. Each one creates a new Python file in backend/ and registers endpoints in main.py. Don't break existing endpoints.

1. ADS-B AIRCRAFT TRACKS (backend/adsb.py + endpoint)
- GET /aircraft endpoint
- On startup or first call, fetch live aircraft from OpenSky Network REST API: https://opensky-network.org/api/states/all?lamin=33.2&lomin=-119.0&lamax=34.2&lomax=-117.5 (Long Beach area bounding box)
- No auth needed for anonymous access
- Parse response into list of: {icao24, callsign, origin_country, lat, lon, altitude_m, velocity_ms, heading, on_ground, last_contact}
- Cache results for 60 seconds to avoid hammering the API
- If the API is unreachable (hackathon wifi), fall back to 8-10 hardcoded realistic aircraft positions in the Long Beach area: 2 Coast Guard MH-65 Dolphins (callsigns CGNR6529, CGNR6517), 1 CBP P-3 Orion (callsign CBP501), and 5 commercial aircraft at altitude. Use realistic coordinates, altitudes, and headings.
- GET /aircraft/proximity/{mmsi} — given a vessel MMSI, return any aircraft within 30nm of that vessel's last known position, sorted by distance

2. OFAC SANCTIONS SCREENING (backend/sanctions.py + endpoint)
- On startup, download OFAC SDN CSV from https://www.treasury.gov/ofac/downloads/sdn.csv OR if unreachable, use a hardcoded set of 20 sanctioned vessel names and 10 sanctioned flag states (Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Venezuela, Myanmar, Belarus, Libya, Somalia)
- GET /sanctions/{mmsi} endpoint — takes an MMSI, looks up the vessel name and flag state from the AIS data, screens against the SDN list by fuzzy name match (difflib.SequenceMatcher, threshold 0.8) and exact flag state match
- Return: {mmsi, vessel_name, flag_state, sanctions_hits: [{list, match_type, match_score, entry_name}], is_flagged: bool, screened_at: timestamp}
- Even if no hits, return is_flagged: false with screened_at — "clean screening" is still an enrichment

3. NOAA WEATHER BUOYS (backend/weather.py + endpoint)
- GET /weather endpoint
- Fetch latest observations from NOAA NDBC Station 46222 (San Pedro) and 46025 (Santa Monica Basin): https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/data/realtime2/46222.txt and 46025.txt
- Parse the latest observation row: wind_speed_mps, wind_direction, wave_height_m, dominant_wave_period, visibility_nm, air_temp_c, water_temp_c, pressure_hpa
- Compute sea_state (Douglas scale) from wave height: 0-0.1m=0, 0.1-0.5m=1, 0.5-1.25m=2, 1.25-2.5m=3, 2.5-4m=4, 4-6m=5, 6-9m=6
- Return both stations plus derived fields
- GET /weather/sensor-impact — return how weather affects each sensor type:
  {"SAR-SPOTLIGHT": {"degradation": 0.0, "note": "SAR unaffected by weather"}, "ELINT-PASS": {"degradation": 0.15, "note": "RF propagation slightly affected by humidity"}, "OPIR-WIDE": {"degradation": 0.6, "note": "Heavy cloud cover degrades IR collection"}}
  Compute degradation from actual weather data (cloud cover/visibility for OPIR, wave height for visual sensors)
- If NDBC is unreachable, fall back to hardcoded realistic weather: wave height 1.2m, wind 12kn NW, visibility 8nm, sea state 3

4. SATELLITE OVERPASS PREDICTION (backend/satellite.py + endpoint)
- GET /overpasses endpoint
- Fetch Sentinel-1 TLE data from Celestrak: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php?GROUP=active&FORMAT=tle — search for SENTINEL-1A and SENTINEL-1B
- If Celestrak is unreachable, use hardcoded TLEs for Sentinel-1A (NORAD 39634)
- Use sgp4 library (pip install sgp4) to propagate the orbit
- Compute the next 3 overpass windows over the Long Beach area (33.7N, -118.3W) within the next 24 hours — an overpass is when the satellite ground track passes within 500km of the target
- Return: [{satellite: "Sentinel-1A", overpass_time_utc, duration_minutes, max_elevation_deg, orbit_direction: "ascending"|"descending", resolution_m: 12.5, swath_km: 250}]
- If sgp4 computation fails, fall back to hardcoded realistic overpass times at 06:30 UTC and 18:15 UTC

5. DEMPSTER-SHAFER FUSION (backend/fusion.py + endpoint)
- GET /fusion/{mmsi} endpoint
- Collects evidence from all sources for a given vessel:
  - AIS: belief mass based on dark event status and duration (dark longer = higher threat belief)
  - ADS-B: if patrol aircraft within 30nm, increase threat belief (they might already be investigating)
  - Sanctions: if flagged, high threat belief; if clean, slight reduction
  - Weather: affects sensor confidence but not threat directly
  - Satellite: next overpass time (informational, feeds into recommendation)
  - Intent classifier: use existing /intent result
  - Triage: use existing /triage score
- Implement Dempster-Shafer combination rule: for each source, define belief mass function m(threat), m(not_threat), m(uncertain). Combine all sources pairwise using DS rule: m12(A) = sum(m1(B)*m2(C) where B∩C=A) / (1 - sum(m1(B)*m2(C) where B∩C=∅))
- Return: {mmsi, sources: [{type, status, confidence, detail, timestamp}], fused_threat_belief, fused_safe_belief, fused_uncertainty, fusion_method: "Dempster-Shafer", recommendation: str}
- Recommendation logic: if fused_threat_belief > 0.7: "IMMEDIATE SENSOR TASKING", elif > 0.4: "ELEVATED MONITORING", else: "ROUTINE TRACKING"

Install any needed packages: pip install sgp4 --break-system-packages. All modules should handle network failures gracefully with hardcoded fallbacks so the demo never breaks.
